question: Stage I seminoma after radical inguinal orchidectomy is typically managed with adjuvant radiotherapy to the para-aortic lymph nodes or single-agent carboplatin, and has an excellent cure rate exceeding 95%.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Seminoma is exquisitely radiosensitive and chemosensitive; stage I disease after orchidectomy is treated with surveillance, adjuvant carboplatin (x1 cycle), or limited-field para-aortic radiotherapy — all achieve >95% disease-free survival.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Stage I seminoma has a >95% cure rate after orchidectomy; adjuvant options include surveillance, single-dose carboplatin, or para-aortic radiotherapy. Seminoma is uniquely radiosensitive — radiotherapy or carboplatin eliminates occult nodal disease.
